Anyone can look at MAs, support and resistance, volume profile, price/sales ratio, etc. But the way in which we feel, see, and ultimately execute on that information is where the major difference between the good and the great lies.

The risk of being bearish and shorting btc down here is less so losing money shorting + missing the initial long off the lows; the bigger risk is being meanigfully wrong footed to the point your ego doubles down and defaults to pessimism and seeks to fade subsequent moves as we move out of a bear market, arguably the most +ev spot in cycles.

As I painfully learned through experience, one of the biggest flaws of discretionary trading: if the ego is in control, you'll only see what the ego wants to see. You'll find the lines on charts or narratives that fit your bias.

I've found that a good way to spot if the ego is in the driving seat is how you initially feel when you see something that counters your current "view/bias". Do you feel triggered, insulted, or driven to mock those views? If so, your ego is likely in control, feeling the need to defend itself. Which, should you end up being wrongfooted, becomes very problematic.

@0xaporia had a very good tweet on this (https://t.co/RtWfGZch8T)

Which is why it makes a ton of sense to have breaks after a winning streak, to reset and keep the ego in check. Another painful learning experience over previous years, but one which I am very grateful for.

Ultimately, every day is a good day to work on creating inner stillness. fertile grounds for flow state. Awareness and fluidity are imperative.

The ego isn't capable of genius.

I think it's important to state which side of the book the liquidation event took place on and what the market context was at the time.

Short cascades that follow a market context with the types of characteristics we've seen recently, including but not exclusive to: structure, volume, and realised + implied vol, are actually very rare and, historically speaking, don't quickly retrace; i.e., the move out of the FTX low and the move in late 2023.

Secondly, Trump didn't mention a thing about gold yesterday, yet it added > $1T to its market cap following the Treasury announcement. So I think to isolate this move to something "Trump said" is somewhat missing the forest for the trees.

Also, all of Trump's historic announcements were around a later-cycle, top-heavy market; this backdrop couldn't be further from that.
